title: Student Transportation Services Rider Terms: One Open Transportation Assignment per Student and School Year
content:
**Clause.** Under Student Transportation Services a household may hold transportation assignments for any number of its students, and each assignment covers one student for one school year. An application is accepted only when the student has no other transportation assignment for the same school year in status applied, active or riding suspended. A student whose situation changes to another transportation type keeps riding on the open assignment until it ends and then applies under the new type; the two never run at the same time.

**Limits.** No limit applies to the number of assignments a household holds. Each student holds at most 1 open assignment per school year.

## What the records must show

The test is made on the district's own transportation assignment records, matched by student and school year, never on the family's account of them.

| The student's other assignment for the same school year | Effect on the new application |
|---|---|
| none | may be accepted |
| applied, active or riding suspended | not accepted |
| denied, ended or cancelled only | does not block the application |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A household applies for bus service for three children for the same school year. Each child receives an own assignment; one child's assignment never blocks a sibling's application.
- A rider on a Courtesy Rider Permit (Annual) moves into the area of another transportation type. The courtesy assignment keeps running until it ends; only then is an application under the new type accepted, so the two assignments are never open together.
- An assignment from the previous school year that is still marked active does not block an application for the new school year, because the test compares assignments of the same school year.
